name: llm-d
description: Agent skills for deploying, benchmarking, and tuning llm-d on Kubernetes and OpenShift.

plugins.name: llm-d-all
plugins.description: Install every llm-d skill at once. Ships no skills of its own, it only pulls in the eight individual plugins, so it can be combined with them without duplicating anything.

plugins.name: create-gke-infra-llm-d
plugins.description: Create or prepare GKE infrastructure (cluster, GPU node pools, RDMA/RoCE networking, DRA and DRANET drivers, Gateway API prerequisites) so that an llm-d stack can be deployed on it. Use this skill when users want to provision a new GKE cluster for llm-d, or make an existing GKE cluster llm-d-ready, especially for prefill/decode disaggregation or wide expert parallelism which require RDMA. Stops at a cluster that is ready for llm-d: install deploy-llm-d (config already decided) or llm-d-autoconfig (config to be recommended) to deploy onto it.

plugins.name: llm-d-autoconfig
plugins.description: Configure an EPP EndpointPickerConfig for an llm-d deployment based on workload + SLA inputs, then optionally deploy it to the user's cluster. Activate when the user asks about configuring llm-d, setting up the inference scheduler, tuning EPP plugins, choosing what config to use for a model or workload, or deploying llm-d. Owns config generation and its own deploy path; install the single-purpose plugins (deploy-llm-d, run-llm-d-benchmark, teardown-llm-d, configure-wva-autoscaling-llm-d) for standalone operations on a config you already have.

plugins.name: deploy-llm-d
plugins.description: Configure and deploy an llm-d stack on an existing Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster by driving the machine-readable guide.yaml of a Well-Lit Path guide (llm-d v1.0 and later). Use this skill when users want to deploy, verify, or customize llm-d from a guide they have already chosen.

plugins.name: run-llm-d-benchmark
plugins.description: Benchmark an already-deployed llm-d stack using the llmdbenchmark CLI, either following a named guide (e.g. optimized-baseline, pd-disaggregation) or using a custom workload profile against any inference endpoint. Use it to measure performance (TTFT, throughput, ITL), validate a deployment under load, or run inference-perf/guidellm/vllm-benchmark. Expects an endpoint to already exist; install deploy-llm-d if you also need to stand one up.

plugins.name: compare-llm-d-configurations
plugins.description: Compare the benchmark performance of two llm-d stack configurations end-to-end. For each configuration, deploys the stack, runs a benchmark, tears down, then generates a side-by-side results comparison. If one configuration was already benchmarked previously, only the new one is deployed and benchmarked, and its results are compared against the existing ones. Use it to A/B test llm-d configurations, compare against a baseline with no llm-d Inference Scheduler, compare models or serving strategies, evaluate the effect of a configuration change, or compare a new run against a previous one. Drives the deploy, benchmark, and teardown skills directly, so installing it also installs deploy-llm-d, run-llm-d-benchmark, and teardown-llm-d.

plugins.name: configure-wva-autoscaling-llm-d
plugins.description: Configure and deploy Workload Variant Autoscaler (WVA) for llm-d inference deployments. Guides users through namespace selection, WVA repo location, configuration (with presets or custom values), deployment via Makefile + kubectl apply, and verification. Produces a reusable deployment script.

plugins.name: clear-kv-cache-tiers-in-llm-d-deployment
plugins.description: Clears all KV / prefix cache tiers (GPU, CPU, and FS offload) on every vLLM pod in an llm-d deployment for a clean state, including both roles of a disaggregated prefill/decode setup. Use it to flush the cache, reset vLLM state, or start fresh before a test run. Prefers the /reset_prefix_cache API and falls back to pod restart. Acts on an already deployed stack; pairs with run-llm-d-benchmark for clean-cache benchmark runs.

plugins.name: teardown-llm-d
plugins.description: Tears down, removes, cleans up, or undeploys a deployed llm-d stack on Kubernetes: remove an llm-d deployment, clean up a namespace after inference workloads, uninstall helm releases for llm-d, or free up cluster resources used by llm-d. Also handles partial cleanup (e.g. remove only the model service, keep the gateway). Supports both Helm-based and Kustomize-based deployments.
